messages:
jess (Maplebridge): Hey team — since yesterday ~18:00 UTC our /v1/generate calls have p99 around 7.2s (baseline ~400-600ms). We also saw several 429s and occasional 500s. Example trace: rb-20260312-abc123. Any quick guidance?

Alex C: Sorry about that, escalating now. Are you on Hosted or Dedicated? Region and model name? @Maria S fyi.

jess (Maplebridge): Hosted, eu-west-1, model=redwood/long-optim:1. Pinned to that model. One request id that hit 12s: rb-20260312-abc123. Small curl to repro:

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-maple-..." 
  -d '{"model":"redwood/long-optim:1","input":"Summarize...","max_tokens":512}'
```

Maria S: Looking at infra metrics now. I can see a cluster-wide p99 spike in eu-west-1 at ~18:05 that aligns with autoscaler activity — a couple of serving pods were recycled due to OOM. There are also per-tenant rate-limiter hits for Maplebridge (lots of soft 429s, queuing increasing).

ops-bot: [ALERT] tenant_rate_limit_exceeded Maplebridge at 2026-03-12T18:05:17Z (count=412)

Sam R: From runtime traces: we have extremely high KV cache evictions on the redwood/long-optim shards serving eu-west-1 at the same time. That causes cache warmness loss and huge token latency on some requests. Correlating with network logs, I see a noisy IP (52.23.44.101) issuing >300 req/s against the embedding endpoint in the same region. Also seeing a different tenant "glitzco" doing very large embedding batches that spike memory.

Alex C: Sounds like a noisy neighbor + eviction cascade. Immediate options: 1) apply a temporary bespoke allowlist for Maplebridge to exempt from soft-throttle and give short burst capacity; 2) pin/split Maplebridge traffic to warm serving pods while we mitigate the noisy tenant. Thoughts @Maria S?

Maria S: Agree on short-term allowlist+bump. We should limit TTL (30m) and avoid starving others. Proposed allowlist rule: tenant=maplebridge, concurrency=6, burst=100, ttl=30m, and pin 2 warm pods for their model. I'll coordinate with infra.

infra: Applying allowlist now. Command: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-config/api/allowlists \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer internal-svc-token" \\n  -d '{"tenant":"maplebridge","concurrency":6,"burst":100,"ttl":"30m"}'
```

deploy-bot: allowlist applied to tenant=maplebridge by infra at 2026-03-12T18:28:41Z — rollout success :white_check_mark:

Alex C: @jess can you confirm if you're seeing any improvement after the allowlist?

jess (Maplebridge): Wow — p99 dropped to ~850ms within 2 minutes. p95 back to ~350ms. Huge improvement, thank you!! :pray:

Maria S: Good. Root cause partial: glitzco scheduled a huge one-off embedding job without burst controls; their pattern was many parallel large batches causing memory pressure and KV evictions. Also the noisy IP was hammering endpoints and tripping per-IP protections. Created internal ticket INF-4721 to follow up with platform/CS to throttle glitzco.

Sam R: Longer-term recommendations:
- Enforce per-tenant KV cache quotas and eviction budgets.
- Backpressure on large embedding-batch requests (reject or rate-limit huge batch sizes).
- Fair-share routing to avoid single-tenant noise bringing down shared shards.
- Per-IP soft-blocking for clearly abusive IPs (like 52.23.44.101).
I'll draft an RFC for these and include perf numbers.

Alex C: Action items:
- Sam R -> RFC for per-tenant quotas and router fair-share (due EOW).
- Maria S -> patch rate-limiter to support transient allowlists + add dashboard for allowlisted tenants (24h).
- infra -> add a UI entry for manual allowlist + TTLs (48h).
- CS -> contact glitzco CSM about scheduled embedding jobs and implement per-tenant burst policy (ticket INF-4721).
- billing -> review credits for Maplebridge for the surge hour.

billing: We'll offer Maplebridge a goodwill credit of 25% for the impacted hour. Jess, confirm if you'd like to accept that or discuss.

jess (Maplebridge): Yes please, that'd be great, thanks.

Maria S: Follow-up notes: we should also consider adding a blackbox monitor for sudden KV eviction rate increases and tie that to autoscaler heuristics. Putting that on infra backlog.

Sam R: Also found trace sample: ``runtime:evict_count: 842`` and aligned p99 spike. Including that in RFC.

Alex C: Summary for Maplebridge: applied temporary allowlist + pinned warm pods -> p99 reduced from ~7.2s to ~850ms. Root cause: noisy tenant embedding bursts + abusive IP causing KV cache eviction cascade. Longer-term fixes noted and tickets created.

jess (Maplebridge): Appreciate the quick help — please keep me posted when the follow-ups are scheduled.

Maria S: Will do. Closing this thread once RFC/tickets PRs are linked. :thumbsup:
